data.title: HPE stock declines 8% on Monday: here's why
data.description:
Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) shares fell 8% on Monday after Evercore ISI downgraded the stock to In Line from Outperform, citing its sharp recent rally and more balanced risk-reward profile.

The brokerage maintained its $65 price target.

HPE shares closed at $62.08 on Friday, Sept. 11, after gaining 15% over the previous five trading sessions and 184% over the past six months.

According to Evercore analyst Amit Daryanani, the stock had risen 158.5% year to date, compared with an 11.9% gain for the S&P 500.

HPE was also up 37.6% in the third quarter, while the benchmark index had gained 2.1%.

Evercore says HPE shares are fairly valued

Daryanani said the downgrade reflected the recent appreciation in HPE’s share price.

The stock was trading at 13 times projected fiscal 2027 earnings, compared with its five-year average of eight times.

“Given the stock now trading at 13x FY27 P/E versus its five-year average of 8x and 14x EV/’27 FCF, in line with its historical average, we believe shares are fairly valued at current levels,” Daryanani wrote in a note to clients.

Evercore said the company’s recent re-rating was supported by fundamental improvements.

The brokerage credited HPE management with strong execution during the first year of integrating Juniper Networks, particularly amid challenging supply conditions.

HPE shares have gained 192% since the Juniper acquisition closed, according to Evercore.

However, the firm said the setup could become more difficult from this point, with fewer immediate catalysts available to support another expansion in the stock’s valuation multiple.

Juniper integration and networking margins remain key

Evercore identified three developments that could make it more constructive on HPE shares.

The first is continued progress in integrating Juniper Networks, particularly if the integration leads to higher margins.

The second involves the company’s business mix and margin quality.

Evercore noted that cloud and artificial intelligence activities generate lower margins than networking equipment.

The third potential catalyst is any benefit from HPE’s Helios opportunity.

The brokerage expects those potential tailwinds to emerge primarily during fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028.

Networking remains particularly important to HPE’s profitability, accounting for more than half of segment operating profit.

Although networking orders increased 36% in the July quarter, pro forma revenue rose 10%, trailing the growth reported by Cisco and Arista, according to Evercore.

HPE faces a tougher setup after strong rally

Evercore said HPE’s recent performance had been justified by improvements in execution and the Juniper integration.

Nevertheless, the firm believes further gains could depend on stronger networking supply conditions and additional margin improvement.

“From here, however, we see a tougher setup,” Daryanani wrote, adding that the balance between potential returns and risks had become more even.

“With risk/reward more balanced at current levels, we are moving to the sidelines with an In Line rating,” he said.

data.title: Nvidia stock: Should investors buy the dip amid AI slowdown fears?
data.description:
Nvidia stock NVDA fell nearly 3% on Monday as concerns over the pace of artificial intelligence development triggered a selloff in AI-related equities.

The decline came after executives at major AI companies called for a slower approach to advancing increasingly capable models.

The broader market also weakened, with the S&P 500 falling 0.33%, the Nasdaq Composite declining 0.38% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average losing 0.12%.

The selloff has raised questions over whether investors should buy the dip in Nvidia, wait for further clarity or reduce their exposure to the chipmaker.

AI slowdown concerns weigh on Nvidia stock

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for AI companies to slow the rate at which they advance model capabilities in a lengthy essay published on X on Saturday.

He cited growing concerns about the potential misuse of artificial intelligence.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and xAI chief Elon Musk said they agreed with Amodei's proposal.

Altman also said OpenAI would not proceed with an initial public offering this year, citing safety concerns.

The comments have prompted investors to reassess the rapid expansion of AI development and the substantial spending that has supported demand for advanced computing infrastructure.

A slower pace of AI development could potentially reduce the need for heavy investment in the technology.

That would create a risk for chipmakers such as Nvidia, whose business has benefited from the expansion of AI infrastructure.

Bernstein analysts led by Stacy Rasgon said the developments could further depress sentiment across the semiconductor sector, which had already been recovering after falling roughly 19% from its June peak.

Bernstein says buy weakness in Nvidia

Despite the recent pressure, Bernstein reiterated its Outperform ratings on Nvidia and Broadcom and recommended buying weakness in both stocks.

The analysts argued that a slowdown in the pace of AI development does not necessarily mean a slowdown in spending.

They noted that Amodei had not called for a halt to AI training, but rather a shift from an extremely fast pace to a somewhat slower one.

Bernstein said such a pace could still represent significant growth for the industry. The firm also pointed to rising demand from AI inference and agentic applications.

The analysts noted that there is already insufficient computing capacity to meet demand for even existing AI models, suggesting that infrastructure requirements could remain substantial despite concerns over the pace of model development.

Anthropic's own spending also provides context for the debate.

According to The Information, the company agreed to 14.8 gigawatts of computing capacity involving approximately $517 billion in commitments over the 11 months through August.

The Financial Times also reported that Anthropic expects a second consecutive quarter of adjusted operating profit, with inference gross margins exceeding 80% before distribution costs.

Nvidia's broader AI strategy offers support

Nvidia has been seeking to reduce its dependence on a small number of major customers by supporting a wider AI ecosystem.

The company has invested in startups and backed open-source AI models, which users can download and modify.

Earlier this month, Nvidia agreed to acquire open-source AI development platform Hugging Face in a $12.9 billion deal, according to the report.

The chipmaker also has customers whose AI ambitions may continue regardless of calls for slower development.

Musk, for example, has said SpaceX is highly confident it will launch Nvidia-powered AI servers in space next year.

SpaceX has previously indicated that it plans to use Nvidia hardware for orbital data centres, potentially addressing some of the land and power constraints facing conventional facilities.

However, the economic viability of orbital data centres remains subject to skepticism.

data.title: Why is Oracle stock falling 4% today?
data.description:
Oracle shares ORCL fell 4.2% on Monday after co-founder Larry Ellison reversed plans to sell as much as $7.5 billion of his stake, while the company faces rising debt and another round of layoffs linked to its artificial intelligence infrastructure spending.

Oracle said Saturday that Ellison had abandoned the planned sale, one day after the company disclosed his trading plans.

The company said, “No Oracle stock was sold under that plan, and he has no other plans to sell any of his Oracle stock.”

The development came after a Friday securities filing revealed that Ellison had adopted a plan on June 22 to sell as many as 50 million Oracle shares, valued at roughly $7.5 billion based on recent prices.

The filing said the sales were expected to be completed by Oct. 24.

Ellison reverses planned Oracle share sale

Ellison has maintained a substantial stake in Oracle since the 1970s and remains one of the company's largest shareholders.

However, much of his wealth is tied to the stock.

A Wall Street Journal analysis found that about 24% of Ellison's roughly $200 billion net worth had been pledged as collateral.

He has also pledged more than $40 billion to support his son David Ellison's hostile bid for Warner Bros. in a deal valued at nearly $80 billion.

Ellison previously sold nearly $900 million of Oracle stock in January 2001, shortly before the company's shares fell almost 22% following lower-than-expected earnings.

He later agreed to pay $100 million to charity to settle an insider-trading lawsuit brought by shareholders.

Oracle ramps up AI spending and debt

Oracle is simultaneously pursuing an aggressive expansion of its AI infrastructure business.

The company plans to raise as much as $50 billion this year through stock and debt sales to finance data centres designed to handle expected growth in artificial intelligence computing.

Morgan Stanley credit analysts expect Oracle will require at least another $100 billion in financing during 2027 and the first half of 2028.

The company's rising debt burden has contributed to pressure on its shares this year.

Oracle stock has fallen more than 23% in 2026, while the technology-heavy Nasdaq has gained more than 13%.

Oracle reported $28.5 billion in first-quarter capital expenditures, up sharply from $8.5 billion a year earlier.

It also maintained its fiscal 2027 capital expenditure forecast at between $90 billion and $95 billion.

Layoffs add to pressure on Oracle

Oracle has also started another round of layoffs, said a Business insider report citing people affected by the cuts and an email reviewed by the publication.

The company told affected employees that their positions were being eliminated as part of a broader organisational change.

Oracle's workforce had already declined by 21,000 employees, or 13%, during the fiscal year ended May 31, according to a recent filing.

Oracle had around 141,000 employees before the latest round of cuts.

The layoffs come as the company continues to spend heavily on AI infrastructure.

While Wall Street remains uncertain about whether those investments will generate sufficient returns, Oracle's latest earnings report showed some positive developments, including cloud growth.

data.title: Can HYPE reclaim $90 after bouncing from $77?
data.description:
HYPE has climbed more than 3% over the past 24 hours, rebounding from around $77 to trade near $81 on Sept. 14.

Much of this buying followed after market reports highlighted that Hyperliquid L1 had moved from eighth to seventh in chain total value locked rankings, overtaking Arbitrum.

Both networks were at roughly $1.40 billion in TVL at the time.

HYPE has climbed more than 3% over the past 24 hours, rebounding from around $77 to trade near $81 on Sept. 14.

Much of the buying followed market reports that Hyperliquid L1 had moved from eighth to seventh in chain total value locked rankings, overtaking Arbitrum.

Both networks were at roughly $1.40 billion in TVL at the time.

Total value locked across the Hyperliquid protocol stood at $6.73 billion, up 11.6% over the past 30 days, according to MSB Intel.

Meanwhile, Hyperliquid’s efforts to gain access to the US derivatives market have remained in focus withing trading circles. 

Kraken parent Payward has proposed a structure under which its Bitnomial subsidiary would offer registered US users crypto perpetual futures linked to markets on Hyperliquid’s decentralised exchange and Layer 1 network, Bloomberg reported in late August. 

Payward has presented the proposed structure to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, although regulatory approval remains pending.

The proposal followed discussions involving Hyperliquid representatives and both the CFTC and Securities and Exchange Commission over possible routes for regulated US firms to offer perpetual futures that trade, clear and settle on Hyperliquid’s blockchain. 

Options under discussion have included regulatory guidance, exemptions and no-action relief, according to The Information.

Regulatory activity around perpetual futures continued into September. 

On Sept. 9, the Hyperliquid Policy Center filed an amicus brief supporting the CFTC in a lawsuit brought by CME Group over the regulator’s decision to allow perpetual futures in the US market.

The group asked the court to dismiss CME’s case.

HYPE’s recovery after the Sept. 6 token unlock has provided another factor behind the latest price move. 

The unlock released 433,419 HYPE allocated to core contributors, equal to 0.19% of the floating supply at the time, creating the potential for selling as previously locked tokens became available.

HYPE fell from its September high near $89 to around $77 but has since returned above $80, showing that buyers have absorbed enough of the available supply to reverse part of the decline. 

The token remains roughly 9% down over the past seven days.

HYPE price analysis

HYPE is trading around $80.85 on the 4-hour chart after bouncing from the $77 area.

Price has moved above the 20-period exponential moving average at $79.82, while the 200 EMA sits lower at $76.92.

The 100 EMA at $80.91 and 50 EMA at $81.27 now sit directly above the price. 

A 4-hour close above $81.27 would clear both averages and could open a move towards $84. A break above $84 would put $86 in view, followed by the September high around $89.

The 4-hour Commodity Channel Index has climbed to around 104 after spending much of the recent decline below zero. 

Its EMA remains near -23. The move above +100 shows that buying momentum has returned on the 4-hour timeframe, but HYPE has yet to clear the $80.91-$81.27 resistance formed by the two EMAs.

On the daily chart, HYPE is trading near $80.71 and remains below its nine-day simple moving average at $81.96. See below.

The SMA sits close to the resistance already visible on the 4-hour chart, placing the main short-term barrier between roughly $81 and $82.

Daily Relative Strength Index stands at 53.8 after falling from above 70 during HYPE’s move towards $89. RSI remains above 50 but below its moving average at 59.8. 

A return above 60 alongside a price break over $82 would support a move towards $84 and $86, with $88-$89 above them.

If HYPE falls back below the 4-hour 20 EMA at $79.82, the next support sits around $78. 

The 200 EMA at $76.92 lines up closely with the recent $77 low, making $76.90-$77 the main support below it. A break under that area could send HYPE towards $74-$75.

data.title: Bitget marks 8 years with UEX expansion across global markets
data.description:
Bitget is marking its eighth anniversary with a focus on expanding its Universal Exchange (UEX) strategy across crypto, traditional financial markets and institutional trading.

The Seychelles-based crypto platform said non-crypto assets accounted for as much as 40% of its total trading volume over the past year.

Trading in traditional finance perpetual contracts and contracts for difference (CFDs) also surpassed $10 billion in daily volume at its peak.

The company is entering its ninth year under the theme “8uilt for Perfect Trades,” as it seeks to broaden the range of markets available on its platform.

Bitget expands UEX offering

Over the past year, Bitget launched stock perpetual contracts, US stock options and Hong Kong stock Quanto contracts as part of its push beyond crypto markets.

The company also said its rToken product surpassed $100 million in assets under management within five weeks and has since recorded more than 3 million cumulative transactions.

According to Bitget, one in four new users now starts their trading journey with rToken.

Bitget has also expanded its use of artificial intelligence in trading through AI Playbook, which the company describes as an autonomous trading agent.

“Crypto and traditional markets are converging, AI is changing the trading experience, and institutional participation is accelerating,” Bitget CEO Gracy Chen said.

Chen added that "UEX is our bet on where all of that is heading, and the next chapter for Bitget will be much bigger than crypto alone."

Security and institutional trading in focus

Bitget said it plans to expand its Proof of Reserves coverage from four to 24 verifiable assets as part of its eighth-anniversary initiatives.

The company's Protection Fund had an average valuation of approximately $382 million in August 2026.

Bitget said the expansion of its asset offering would be accompanied by continued investment in security, market integrity and compliance.

Institutional trading is also expected to remain a priority during the company's ninth year.

As of the second quarter of 2026, institutional client net assets had increased 45% from the end of 2025, according to Bitget.

The number of core active market makers also increased from 90 to 248 firms.

The company said it plans to strengthen execution quality, API and quantitative trading infrastructure, institutional services and cross-asset account capabilities.

Bitget prepares for its ninth year

Bitget's eighth-anniversary celebrations will include KCGI 2026, which features a 3 million USDT prize pool, as well as VIP programmes, community activities and offline events across multiple regions.

The company said its focus for the next stage remains on improving the trading experience while expanding access to a broader range of markets.

Bitget currently says it serves more than 125 million users and offers access to more than 2 million crypto tokens, alongside tokenised stocks, ETFs, commodities, foreign exchange and precious metals including gold.

As it enters its ninth year, Bitget is positioning UEX as the central part of its strategy to bring crypto and traditional markets together on a single trading platform.

data.title: KOSPI vs Nikkei: Asia’s AI trade fractures ahead of Fed and BOJ decisions
data.description:
Asian stocks diverged on Tuesday as South Korea’s KOSPI struggled to shake off pressure on semiconductor shares while Japan’s Nikkei 225 recovered, leaving the region’s two most AI-sensitive markets moving in opposite directions ahead of key US and Japanese rate decisions.

The KOSPI fell as much as 0.76% in early Seoul trading before paring most of the decline, extending a difficult stretch after Monday’s sharp technology sell-off.

The Nikkei 225, by contrast, rose about 0.8% in later trade as SoftBank Group rebounded strongly and helped offset weakness elsewhere in the Japanese market.

The split came as investors assessed another rise in crude oil, elevated global bond yields and calls from technology executives for a slower pace of frontier AI development.

MSCI’s broad Asia-Pacific gauge outside Japan was little changed, while Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 fell and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng also traded lower.

KOSPI remains exposed to the AI trade

South Korea remains particularly sensitive to any reassessment of AI spending because Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix carry heavy weight in the KOSPI and sit at the centre of the global memory-chip supply chain.

Samsung slipped in early trade while SK Hynix moved around the flat line, following Monday’s steep semiconductor losses.

Foreign investors were net sellers for a fifth straight session early Tuesday, adding another layer of pressure to the index.

Kiwoom Securities analyst Han Ji-young told Yonhap that part of the overnight weakness in US chip shares had already been reflected in Monday’s Korean sell-off, leaving room for some recovery as investors reassessed valuations.

Nikkei 225 gets a lift from SoftBank

Japan’s Nikkei 225 reversed early losses as SoftBank Group rallied more than 8%, giving the price-weighted benchmark an outsized boost.

Kioxia also advanced, helping Japanese technology shares recover some ground after the previous session’s rout.

The rebound does not remove the macro pressure on Japanese equities.

The yen traded around 154.6 per dollar, while Japan’s 10-year government bond yield hovered near 3% as investors prepared for the Bank of Japan’s decision on Friday.

The BOJ is widely expected to raise its policy rate by 25 basis points to 1.25%, the highest level in 31 years.

Markets will focus less on the widely anticipated move than on Governor Kazuo Ueda’s guidance on how quickly further tightening could follow.

Oil and rates keep both markets on edge

Crude remained another source of risk. Brent traded near $107 a barrel and US crude above $102 after renewed attacks on Saudi infrastructure revived concern about supply disruptions.

Higher energy costs are particularly uncomfortable for import-dependent Japan and South Korea because they can lift inflation while squeezing corporate margins.

US Treasury yields have added to that pressure, with the 10-year yield briefly touching 5%.

Markets are assigning roughly a 90% chance to a quarter-point Federal Reserve increase on Wednesday, which would be the first rate rise in roughly three years.

JPMorgan strategist Mislav Matejka argued that a measured Fed hike need not derail equities if earnings remain strong, but the combination of expensive oil, elevated yields and uncertainty around AI spending leaves the KOSPI and Nikkei 225 vulnerable to sharp swings through the rest of the week.

data.title: Kioxia share price on edge as it plans a $10 billion ADR US listing
data.description:
Kioxia share price remained under pressure on Tuesday as companies in the artificial intelligence (AI) industry slip. It was trading at ¥51,720, down modestly from last week’s high of ¥61,300. This stock will be in the spotlight as the company plans to follow in SK Hynix’s footsteps by launching a US listing.

Kioxia could raise $10 billion for expansion

Kioxia Holdings, the fourth biggest company in Japan, has been one of the top beneficiaries of the artificial intelligence boom. This boom has led to a surge in data center buildup, which has led to more demand for storage solutions as the amount of data rises.

Kioxia has benefited from this demand because of its strong presence in the industry, where it sells storage devices. Its top clients, including companies like Apple, Microsoft, and Google have all committed to keep spending. 

Now, the company is plotting to raise $10 billion by listing its shares in the United States. To do that, it is working with companies like Bank of America, Goldman Sachs, and JPMorgan on an offering that may happen next year. 

The firm plans to use the funds to build its balance sheet and gain liquidity in the United States. One way that this listing will help it is by letting it be listed in key semiconductor indices. The company told Bloomberg:

“Kioxoa is preparing to list American Depositary Shares representing its common shares on a US stock exchange to steadily and sustainably increase corporate value.”

Kioxia will become the second big foreign name to list in the United States. SK Hynix, the biggest company in the high bandwidth memory (HBM) industry, raised $26.5 billion in a listing in July. Its US stock initially dropped to $124.6 and then bounced back to nearly $200 last week.

Kioxia’s business is thriving

Kioxia Holdings’ business is doing well as demand for its memory devices continues to grow. Its most recent results showed that its revenue soared to over ¥1.76 trillion from ¥1 trillion in the first quarter of the year. Most of this revenue came from its SSD and storage business, which made ¥1.17 trillion, while its smart devices made over ¥525 billion.

As a result, the company’s profit jumped to ¥842 billion. This growth mirrored that of other top companies in the memory industry, including SanDisk, which it has a joint venture with. As a result, the company has started to repurchase its shares. It announced a 30 million share buyback, which is equivalent to 5.47% of its outstanding shares.

Kioxia stock price technical analysis

The daily chart shows that the Kioxia stock has retreated substantially in the past few months. It slumped from a high of ¥112,750 in June to the current ¥51,350. 

The stock has slumped below the 50-day Exponential Moving Average (EMA). Also, it has formed a symmetrical triangle whose two lines are now nearing their confluence. This triangle formed after the stock made a big drop, a sign that it is part of a bearish pennant pattern.

Therefore, the stock will likely remain under pressure, with the next key target to watch being at ¥35,970, its lowest level on July 30. A move above the upper side of the triangle will invalidate the bearish outlook.

data.title: Samsung and SK Hynix defy a 6% US chip rout: what is Korea seeing differently
data.description:
Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix rose in Seoul on Tuesday, resisting the semiconductor selloff that swept Wall Street overnight as investors reassessed whether calls to slow artificial intelligence development imply weaker chip demand.

Samsung gained 0.7% and SK Hynix advanced 1.82% by 11:20 a.m., while the KOSPI was little changed.

The moves followed a 5% slide in the PHLX Semiconductor Index on Monday, when AI-linked chipmakers were hit by fears that a slower pace of frontier-model development could curb infrastructure spending.

The divergence is less dramatic than it appears, as Korean memory stocks had already absorbed much of the shock a session earlier.

Korea priced the AI scare first

Samsung fell 4.05% on Monday and SK Hynix dropped 6.35%, helping pull the KOSPI down 3.26%.

Seoul therefore reacted to the AI slowdown debate before Wall Street delivered its own semiconductor selloff.

Tuesday’s rebound suggests investors were unwilling to sell the same concern twice without evidence that orders, server deployments or memory consumption are weakening.

However, it is not a broad vote of confidence, as individual investors sold more than 13 trillion won of Samsung and SK Hynix shares between September 1 and 11, while foreign investors also reduced exposure.

Corporate treasury-share purchases absorbed much of that selling.

Memory shortages complicate the bearish case

The simplest bearish chain is that slower AI development leads to lower capital expenditure, fewer accelerators and ultimately less memory.

But current supply conditions make that relationship less straightforward.

Ben Barringer, global head of technology research at Quilter Cheviot, told CNBC that inference capacity remains constrained even if training and model rollouts slow.

“Demand still far outstrips supply,” he said, arguing that a modest slowdown may not materially damage company revenues.

TrendForce reported this month that DRAM industry revenue jumped 59.5% quarter-on-quarter in the second quarter to nearly $154.73 billion.

It said AI servers are driving demand for HBM and high-capacity server memory while supplier inventories remain historically low.

The research firm also expects server DRAM shortages and elevated pricing to extend into 2027 as capacity shifts towards HBM.

That scarcity is already affecting chip prices. Chinese AI-chip suppliers have raised prices by roughly 20% to 50% on some products as HBM shortages increase costs.

Korea is watching where AI profits move

The bigger Korean investment case is that AI spending may increasingly reward memory suppliers rather than only GPU designers.

“Next year, the center of profit will shift from graphics processing units to memory,” Kim Dong-won, head of research at KB Securities, told the Seoul Economic Daily.

That view helps explain why Samsung and SK Hynix can trade differently from Nvidia and other US semiconductor names.

Their earnings are increasingly leveraged to memory pricing, HBM scarcity and server demand rather than solely to the speed of the next frontier-model release.

The risk is that this distinction eventually disappears.

Christopher Wood, global head of equity strategy at Jefferies, told the Korea Times that the biggest danger is markets deciding companies will not be able to “monetise this capex.”

If hyperscalers conclude their huge AI investments cannot generate adequate returns, spending cuts would eventually hit GPUs, servers and memory alike.

data.title: Netflix stock rises as Evercore raises price target to $110
data.description:
Netflix shares NFLX rose about 4.3% on Monday after Evercore ISI increased its price target on the streaming company to $110 from $100 and reiterated its Outperform rating.

The new target implies roughly 42% upside from Netflix’s previous closing price.

The brokerage cited improving subscriber trends in the United States and Japan, as well as growth opportunities from live events, short-form content and advertising.

Netflix penetration reaches multi-year high in US

Evercore analyst Kutgun Maral said Netflix’s penetration rate reached a multi-year high of 63% in the US.

In Japan, penetration rose to a record 22%, according to the brokerage’s surveys.

Churn intentions also improved in both markets, although customer satisfaction remained a concern in the US.

The findings came from Evercore ISI’s 58th quarterly US subscriber survey and its semi-annual survey in Japan.

The brokerage said the results strengthened its view that Netflix retains strong subscriber engagement and pricing power.

Netflix stock climbed 4.32% in morning trading to $80.74.

The valuation framework was extended to 2028, using 25 times the firm’s 2028 earnings-per-share estimate.

Citi also maintained a Buy rating and a $100 price target in a recent note.

Live events and short-form content offer growth opportunities

Evercore identified live programming as a potential driver of subscriber growth and engagement.

In Japan, 45% of newly surveyed subscribers said they joined Netflix as part of the company’s World Baseball Classic promotion.

The survey also showed that the percentage of users who had watched live events increased to 60% in September from 42% in March.

The brokerage also highlighted Netflix Clips, the company’s short-form video feed.

Around 46% of Japanese respondents and 38% of US respondents said they had scrolled through the feature.

Evercore said live events and short-form videos could support engagement and retention.

The company’s advertising-supported tier was also attracting new and returning subscribers.

Netflix’s margins and buybacks support earnings growth

Netflix’s broader strategy remains focused on growing revenue and operating profit while managing content costs.

Management is targeting an operating margin of 31.5% this year, up from 29.5% last year and 26.5% two years ago.

Content costs increased 11.5% in the first half of 2026, while total viewing hours rose 2% year over year.

The company has also expanded its live programming and added lower-cost content, including video podcasts.

The advertising business is expected to generate approximately $3 billion this year.

A Motley Fool report said advertising could provide further growth through increased ad-supported viewing, new products and improvements to Netflix’s advertising technology.

Netflix also repurchased a record $4.7 billion of its shares in the second quarter. Its board had authorised an additional $25 billion in buybacks, with $27.1 billion remaining under existing authorisations at the end of June.

Evercore described Netflix as a sustainable 20% earnings-per-share growth company, although it expects the company’s catalyst path to become more visible in 2027 rather than 2026.

data.title: AI panic triggers a rally in CrowdStrike stock
data.description:
CrowdStrike (CRWD) stock is ripping higher on Monday morning, defying a broader tech rout, to hit an all-time intraday high of $238.68.

Investors are aggressively bidding up pure-play security firms today following heightened urgency around AI vulnerabilities, propelling CRWD far past the broader software index.

Including today’s gains, CrowdStrike shares are up more than 100% versus the start of this year.

What’s driving CrowdStrike stock higher today?

Urgent safety warnings issued over the weekend by executives across leading artificial intelligence frontier labs like Anthropic and OpenAI sparked a wave of enterprise fear.

Industry leaders cautioned that rapidly evolving autonomous agents and machine-speed AI workflows are expanding the corporate attack surface much faster than traditional IT teams can manage.

Rather than dampening sentiment, the threat profile drove huge sums of institutional capital into specialized cybersecurity firms tasked with securing next-generation software infrastructure.

CRWD stock emerged as a key beneficiary as investors wagered that complex artificial intelligence deployment directly expands mission-critical security spending.

What else is helping CRWD shares rally?

CrowdStrike stock is rallying today also because, as macro uncertainties weighed on semiconductor manufacturers and hardware suppliers, traders executed a notable capital rotation out of hardware and into high-margin software operators.

Software pure-plays equipped with recurring subscription revenues saw immediate inflows – with CrowdStrike, Zscaler, and Palo Alto Networks leading the charge.

Institutional funds are seeking shelter in platform security names whose growth trajectories remain insulated from supply chain friction, hardware cycles, or chip export constraints, making enterprise cybersecurity a top defensible AI trade.

Fal.Con momentum remains a tailwind

Finally, CRWD shares printed a new high as market momentum continues to build on the heels of the recent Fal.Con 2026 annual conference, where executive leadership unveiled Falcon Guardian and SafeMind.

These specialized tools are designed specifically to monitor, audit, and protect autonomous agents operating within corporate cloud networks.

Along with ambitious long-term financial targets including reaching $10 billion in annual recurring revenue (ARR) by the end of this decade and double it again by fiscal 2035, CrowdStrike Holdings looks like an increasingly attractive long-term bet.

How Wall Street recommends playing CrowdStrike

CrowdStrike’s breakout rally underscores a structural shift in enterprise technology: security is no longer an afterthought, but the primary enabler of scale.

By directly addressing the threat profile of autonomous AI agents – while capturing “hardware-to-software” capital flows, CRWD has cemented its market dominance.

As management delivers on its longer-term revenue goals, CRWD stands exceptionally positioned to command the AI-driven cybersecurity era.

Investors should also note that despite massive year-to-date outperformance, Wall Street analysts remain bullish as ever on CrowdStrike for the next 12 months.

According to Barchart, the consensus rating on the cybersecurity giant sits at Moderate Buy, with price targets going as high as $425, indicating potential for another 75% rally from here.
